prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and targets (max 500 words)

Health and social care
- NHS: Cut waiting lists; rapid GP access; guaranteed NHS dentistry. Additional revenue spend in England rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. £2bn primary care capital; increase primary care funding by up to £1.5bn/yr by 2030. Restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn).
- Dentistry: New NHS contract; increase funding to £3bn/yr by 2030; community preventive services.
- Workforce: Pay restoration for junior doctors; improved NHS pay/conditions to aid retention.
- Mental health: Access to evidence-based therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school/college.
- Cancer: National plan to increase early diagnosis (75% stage 1–2 by 2028).
- Assisted dying: Support legal change with safeguards.
- Social care: Free personal care; national pay/career structure; £20bn/yr investment. +£3bn for children’s social care.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes annually; end Right to Buy.
- Renters: Local rent controls; end Section 21 no-fault evictions; longer tenancies; tenant right to demand energy upgrades.
- Retrofit/standards: Ten-year programme including £29bn (home insulation to EPC B), £9bn (low‑carbon heating), £7bn (overheating adaptation), £4bn (public buildings). Mandate Passivhaus-equivalent for new homes; solar and heat pumps on new builds.
- Planning: Protect green spaces/Green Belt; whole‑life carbon assessments; reuse of demolition materials; reduce car dependency.

Energy and industry
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; phased carbon tax from £120/tCO2 to up to £500/t within 10 years.
- Electricity: Wind ~70% by 2030; targets by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, 100GW solar; end onshore wind constraints; community ownership thresholds; support local supply (Local Electricity Bill).
- Grid/storage: Expand grid, interconnectors, offshore networks; scale storage; green hydrogen for industry.
- Nuclear: Stop new projects; phase out existing.
- Skills/transition: Up to £4bn/yr for training; Offshore Energy and Skills Passport.

Economy, tax and public finances
- Public/green investment averaging ~£40bn/yr (energy, retrofits, rail, public transport, active travel, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage).
- Public ownership: Rail, water companies, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Tax: Annual wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align Capital Gains Tax and investment income rates with earnings; remove NI Upper Earnings Limit; reform inheritance tax; carbon tax as above; windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT changes (lower for hospitality/arts; higher for private education/financial services).
- Property: Revalue Council Tax; steps toward Land Value Tax; survey of landholdings.

Work and welfare
- Workers’ rights: Repeal anti‑union laws; day‑one rights; gig workers classed as “workers.”
- Pay: £15/hr minimum wage (support for small firms); 10:1 maximum pay ratio guidance.
- Social security: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; abolish two‑child cap; end five‑week wait; +5% disability benefits; carers’ allowance +10%; maintain real pensions; long‑term goal of Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; protect 30% land/sea by 2030; re‑wet peat; expand woodlands; increase DEFRA/EA/NE budgets; renationalise water; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animal welfare: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; phase out factory farming practices; end routine antibiotics; ban cages.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support for nature‑friendly farming; cut pesticides; expand horticulture; free daily school meals for all children; local food partnerships.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn funding (incl. £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings (RAAC, maintenance); broaden curriculum; end high‑stakes testing; abolish Ofsted; SEND +£5bn.
- Post‑16/FE: +£3bn for sixth form; £12bn for skills/lifelong learning; restore EMA.
- HE: Scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Transport
- Subsidies: Increase to £10bn/yr by end of parliament; free bus travel for under‑18s.
- Investment: +£19bn/5yrs for public transport and active travel; £2.5bn/yr for walking/cycling; rail nationalisation and accelerated electrification; oppose new road building; road pricing over time; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2027; phase out use by 2035; EV scrappage up to £5bn/yr.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Proportional representation; repeal voter ID; elected second chamber; votes at 16; fair party funding; stronger lobbying/think‑tank transparency; defend Human Rights Act and ECHR access.
- Migration/asylum: End “hostile environment”; safe routes; allow work while claims processed; remove spousal income minimums; simplify/at‑cost fees; free NHS access for visa holders.

Culture, media, digital
- £5bn over 5 years for local arts/sport/culture; VAT exemptions for cultural events; media ownership caps (≤20% market); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; AI precautionary regulation; protect creators’ IP.

Justice and policing
- Community‑based policing; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences under 2 years; decriminalise personal drug possession; invest to reduce court backlogs (legal aid, judges, court estate); make misogyny a hate crime; decriminalise sex work.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; pursue EU re‑entry (Customs Union step, free movement, Erasmus); increase aid to 1% GNI by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss and Damage; recognise Palestine; immediate bilateral ceasefire; halt UK arms exports to Israel; sign TPNW and cancel Trident; work within NATO with No First Use objective.
